Follow-up 2026-09-12: the two options are not symmetric, and the source says which way it leans. Not migrating is a deliberate shipped commitment, not an omission: it is item 1 of four in NOTICE_4_0_0_ITEMS (src/commands/upgrade.rs:241), a constant the comment at :238 says is pinned as a slice "so a test can assert the notice still carries every item". Building a migration therefore does not merely add a code path; it falsifies a release note the operator has already published to users and would have to be withdrawn from the notice, and it needs 3.x token material to be decryptable by 4.0.0 code that no longer keeps that format. Rewriting the criterion to match the shipped re-authenticate-once behaviour costs one requirement edit and leaves every other conjunct as graded. The recommendation is the rewrite; the decision is still the operator's, because it changes what MIK-6744 promised. Follow-up 2026-09-13: the asymmetry is now verified at source rather than inferred, and the recommendation is to rewrite the criterion. There is no 3.x store reader and no legacy key-derivation path anywhere in src/personal_accounts/: legacy_migration (mod.rs:207) is propagated by commit.rs:285-299 and written None at repair_tests.rs:179 and nowhere else, so the migration option is not a design alternative but unwritten decryption for key material this release cannot read. Against that, NOTICE_4_0_0_ITEMS (upgrade.rs:241) is pinned as a slice with the comment at :238 stating it is a slice so a test can assert the notice still carries every item, and item 1 is the no-migration promise the operator has already published. Building migration therefore falsifies a test-pinned shipped commitment. An implementing agent declined to write a test for this row on 2026-09-13 and was correct to: a test pinning the shipped behaviour asserts the opposite of the criterion, and a test pinning migration is red by construction. The row stays pending because rewriting a release criterion is a scope decision and is not an agent's to land. Follow-up 2026-09-14: the READABLE half now has a named mechanism, and one recorded reason is corrected. The 3.x single-user store is byte-identical in 4.0.0 -- TokenInfo, storage_key, token_path and default_location in src/oauth/storage.rs are unchanged from v3.5.1 (git show v3.5.1:src/oauth/storage.rs) and it is still a live production read path (src/backend/lifecycle.rs:530). 3.x data is unreachable not because no reader survives but because the KEY changed: v3.5.1 called storage.load(backend_name, http_url) (lifecycle.rs:352/425 -> client), 4.0.0 calls storage.load(&credential_key(), &resource_url) where credential_key() is backend_name + NUL + issuer (src/oauth/client/mod.rs:114 and :386, load at :356), so the SHA-256 filename differs and the 3.x file is never opened; drop_credentials_from_other_issuer (:408) additionally clears in-memory credentials across an issuer change. That is exactly the shipped "re-authenticates once" behaviour and it confirms READABLE is UNMET. It also corrects the 2026-09-13 claim that migration "needs 3.x token material to be decryptable by 4.0.0 code that no longer keeps that format": the legacy record is PLAINTEXT JSON at 0600 (src/oauth/storage.rs:231 writes serde_json::to_string_pretty; seal_bytes encryption belongs to the NEW per-user store only) and the 4.0.0 TokenInfo still parses it, so migration is a filename re-key, not unwritten decryption. That prices the READ side only. The WRITE side is not free: the destination AccountKey (src/personal_accounts/mod.rs:49) is keyed on principal_authority, principal_subject, backend_id, resource and oauth_issuer, and a GrantRecord (:137) additionally requires generation, token_revision, authorization_epoch, descriptor_revision and client_id. A 3.x TokenInfo (src/oauth/storage.rs:20) carries none of the principal fields and none of the generation fields, and its file is keyed on backend_name alone, so migration must invent an attribution it has no source for. It must then land through commit_grant_if (service.rs:342, worker.rs:254), which is itself annotated expect(dead_code, reason = "per-user OAuth scaffolding, deferred to post-4.0.0 backlog MIK-6744/6745/6746"). Migration is therefore a re-key on the read side and an unresolved attribution into a deferred surface on the write side. The recommendation is unchanged -- the blocker is that migration falsifies NOTICE_4_0_0_ITEMS item 1 (src/commands/upgrade.rs:241), a promise already published to operators, which is a scope decision -- but the operator should decide against the true cost rather than against a decryption problem that does not exist.
